title: L'ultima prova dell'amor mio
subtitle: Donna Elvira, Don Giovanni and Leporello: finale from Don Giovanni, Act 2 (No. 24)

passages.label: L'ultima prova dell'amor mio · Da te non chiede quest'alma oppressa
Mi maraviglio! · Ah non deridere · Quasi da piangere · Che vuoi, mio bene?
Che vita cangi! · Cor perfido! · Lascia ch'io mangi
Restati, barbaro! · Se non si muove · Vivan le femmine
Restati, barbaro! (again) · Vivan le femmine (again) · Elvira's scream
Che grido è questo mai? · Leporello, che cos' è?
Allegro molto: Ah! Signor! per carità! · ta, ta, ta · Qualcun batte! (to the end)

licences.notes: Words as printed in the Schirmer vocal score (Cos' è on two notes, maraviglio, perchè, quà; Giovanni's "Io ti deridere!" in bar 50 before "Io te deridere?" in bar 54; the print's "femine" in bar 125, "lamico" in bar 227 and "masconderò" in bar 229, kept because the words must match the score; the libretto has meraviglio, femmine, l'amico, m'asconderò). Bar 1's "-var." (Giovanni and Leporello), the end of "provar" from the previous piece, is not part of this piece's words.

licences.source: G. Schirmer vocal score, New York 1900 (plate 15147, IMSLP #68957), pages 264–273, bars 1–233 of the Act 2 Finale from Elvira's entrance (Allegro assai) to the bar before the double bar and Andante where the Commendatore enters
licences.author: G. Schirmer, piano reduction as printed
licences.notes: Written out from the printed pages: the sung lines and the piano each read by two independent readers, every disagreement settled on the page by a judge, then checked bar by bar and checked again by fresh checkers. Three clear misprints are corrected: piano left hand bar 54 E natural, piano right hand bar 155 A flat, Elvira bar 154 A flat (the held scream). Elvira's small ossia notes (bars 146–147) are left out. Single-chord tremolos (left hand bars 115–124 and elsewhere) are written as held chords. The English singing translation and the stage directions are left out. Bar 1 begins on the downbeat that ends Già la mensa ("-var."). Allegro assai 3/4 in B-flat major bars 1–179; Allegro molto alla breve in F major bars 180–233. Playback tempo: Allegro assai ♩ = 205 (a dotted half ≈ 68) and Allegro molto 𝅗𝅥 = 122 (♩ = 244), about 3:30 in all, the median of five complete recordings with this scene on its own track or tracks (Maazel 1979 3:25, Fricsay 1958 3:26, Giulini 1959 3:30, Haitink 1984 3:37, Böhm 1967 3:42), divided between the sections as in Giulini's, which puts "Che grido è questo mai?" (bar 155) on its own track (2:15 + 1:15). Mozart gives the words Allegro assai and Allegro molto only.
